brief: Verdict ahead of the print: delivery at Vineland and the funding sequence, not revenue.
Kona: IG-backed prepayments plus asset-backed debt is the template; permitting discipline is now a tenant requirement.
changes: Report date: before the US open on 12 November, call 8:00 a.m. ET (company, 30 October).

Stock $129.49 on 6 November, from $299.86 high in June; fell about 15% on 5 November on the Texas moratorium threat and a Bloomberg report that Microsoft tightened oversight of Nebius, IREN and Nscale projects.
$5.0bn converts priced 19 August, $5.75bn closed 24 August with greenshoe (0.50% 2030, 4.50% 2034; conversion about $313-325) and $800mn of older notes swapped for about 15.8mn shares.
$3.5bn 364-day secured Citi facility on 22 October at SOFR+275bp stepping up to 350bp; $775mn asset-backed loan at SOFR+250bp in July.
Targets cut: Citi $324 to $265 (Buy), Piper $237 to $185 (Neutral); BofA Buy $310; Morgan Stanley Equal-weight $144.
checks: Built before results. Report date from company release (30 October). 2Q26 and 3Q25 figures, ARR, prepayment guide, ATM remaining and $ per MW from 6-K exhibits on EDGAR, confirmed by a fresh subagent. Converts, $775mn ABS (matures 31 October 2030) and Citi facility confirmed from company releases. Price $129.49 on 6 November and 5 November -14.9% confirmed (StockAnalysis). FY26 guides (revenue, capex, YE ARR, MW) from 2Q call recap, not reconfirmed. Consensus from Yahoo, Zacks, StockAnalysis, Equibles; TIKR capex and net debt single source. Microsoft oversight from a secondary write-up of Bloomberg; Vineland fine not reconfirmed. No convert quote found.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Nebius for hyperscaler-anchored demand (Microsoft $17.4-19.4bn, Meta up to about $27bn, over $40bn of commitments), a 41% adjusted EBITDA margin and prepayment-heavy funding that makes its credit look unlike CoreWeave's; at $129.49 on 6 November (down from $299.86 in June, about 17% of shares short, Burry publicly short) the market is pricing delivery and funding risk at Vineland and neocloud contagion, not a demand problem.
headline: 3Q26 revenue (consensus about $906mn, +56% QoQ) is not the test: the stock trades on whether Vineland delivers for Microsoft, how the 364-day Citi facility is taken out, and whether the year-end ARR guide of $7-9bn and a first 2027 guide hold.
kona: Nebius shows the funding path a GPU owner can use when its tenants are investment grade: prepayments covering 50-60% of capex, asset-backed loans at SOFR+250-275bp, and converts. If those spreads hold through a neocloud sell-off, hosting an IG-backed GPU owner is a financeable model for Kona; if Microsoft's tighter oversight of third-party sites becomes a pattern, Kona should expect hyperscaler tenants to demand site access, delivery penalties and permitting proof (Vineland was fined over $1mn for 62 unpermitted generators), which favors getting Argentine permits and gas supply fully documented before signing.

name: Nebius

questions.question: Citi's $3.5bn facility is 364-day secured debt at SOFR+275bp stepping to 350bp. How much is drawn, against what collateral, what triggers the step-up, and what takes it out: size, advance rate, date and spread of the asset-backed loan against the $40bn of commitments, compared with $775mn at SOFR+250bp?
questions.why: Tests the funding pillar; a 364-day bridge without a named take-out is the bears' main point.

questions.question: You guided over $9bn of 2026 prepayments with $5.98bn deferred revenue at 30 June. What was collected in 3Q, and how much of second-half capex (about $12-17bn left of the $20-25bn guide) is funded by prepayments versus new debt?
questions.why: Prepayments are what make Nebius's credit different from CoreWeave's.

questions.question: 12.3mn ATM shares remained at 30 June and the August exchange issued about 15.8mn more. How many ATM shares were sold since, at what price, and is equity in the 2027 plan with the stock near $130?
questions.why: Dilution versus debt sets the cost of the next dollar.

questions.question: Vineland had stop-work orders in August, a NJ DEP fine over $1mn for 62 unpermitted generators on 22 September, and Microsoft staff on site per Bloomberg on 5 November. Is any Microsoft tranche late, and are delay credits accruing?
questions.why: Delivery to the anchor customer is the core execution pillar.

questions.question: What were connected and active MW and ARR at 30 September, and are you narrowing the $7-9bn year-end ARR range given 2Q contracts only bill from late 4Q?
questions.why: FY26 revenue consensus already sits near the top of guidance.

questions.question: 2Q D&A of about $260mn was about 45% of revenue against a 41% EBITDA margin. What useful life do you use for Blackwell and Rubin, and what are 2027 revenue, capex (consensus about $29bn) and margin guides?
questions.why: Judges profitability on operating margin, not EBITDA.

sections.body: Full-stack AI GPU cloud; AI cloud was $575mn of $582mn 2Q26 revenue. Revenue = connected MW x price per MW-year (about $20-25mn per MW-year on multi-year deals, $40-50mn short-term, per 2Q call). Funded by customer prepayments, converts, ATM equity, secured and asset-backed debt and operating cash flow. Anchors: Microsoft (Vineland, NJ) and Meta (up to about $27bn, tranches from early 2027).
